title: Basic content measurements: Humanus measures size, structure, sourcing and change; Papyrus stories measure and save-version report them
description:
As an editor (or an agent working for one), I want plain measurements of a draft -- how long it is, how it is built, how well it is sourced, and how much a revision changed -- so that I have numbers to judge a piece by before and after I edit it.

Numbers are guidance, never gates: no fixed limits, nothing blocks on them.

Humanus owns ALL measurement logic (Papyrus has no counting logic): `humanus.measure(text, language, concepts=None)` and `humanus.diff(old_text, new_text, language)`. Deterministic, no model calls, language-aware (zh-Hans counts characters, not words). Concept density takes a concept list as input and is a LATER slice (not built here).

First slice:
- size: word count (characters for zh-Hans), reading time
- structure: sections, longest paragraph, longest sentence, presence/length of headline, dek and blurb when given
- sourcing: links and citations per 500 words, share of paragraphs without any
- change size: words added, removed, rewritten, share of text changed

Papyrus: bump the Humanus pin; `papyrus stories measure` works on a draft file or story id before saving; `stories save-version` prints the measurements and the change against the previous version and stores them on the version record.

```gherkin
Feature: Basic content measurements
  Scenario: A draft is measured before it is saved
    Given a draft file
    When I run "papyrus stories measure" on it
    Then I see its size, structure and sourcing numbers
  Scenario: Saving a version reports and stores the change
    Given a story with a saved version
    When I save a new version
    Then the output shows the measurements and the change against the previous version
    And both are stored on the version record
```

Definition of done: Humanus released and verified by tag and registry; Papyrus PR with feat: title merged into develop on green CI; no Papyrus release cut.
